messages:
maria: Quick sync: we need to lock down 'claiming' semantics for adapters across hosted / dedicated / private. Specifically: who issues the claim, TTLs, how evictions are signaled to clients, and what auth scope the token carries.
ash: My take: single authoritative claim token from control plane. Runtime must renew. If it misses renew window -> immediate eviction.
ken: Single token is fine for hosted/dedicated. For private we need delegated claims (customer-controlled control plane). Suggest token has claim_origin field.
tanvi: Draft proposal: default lease TTL = 90s, renew attempt at ~30s (with jitter +/-20%). Grace window for in-flight streams = 120s. For Dedicated we can use shorter TTL (30s) to free GPUs faster.
maria: Jitter and grace feel right. How do we expose eviction reason to the client app? Need structured machine-readable codes + optional human text.
ash: Suggest adding a header for sync responses: X-Redwood-Claim-Status: renewed|evicted and X-Redwood-Claim-Reason: CAPACITY_PREEMPT|AUTHZ|RESTART. For streaming, emit final control event chunk: 
```
{ "event": "claim_evicted", "reason": "CAPACITY_PREEMPT", "timestamp": 1825009999 }
```
ken: For private (customer control plane not reachable) we can't rely on immediate control-plane-driven events. Runtime should write a local journal entry and expose an audit endpoint /local-journal that control plane pulls when reconnecting.
tanvi: Also add metrics: claim_renew_latency_ms histogram, claim_evictions_total{reason,mode,tenant}. That will help on-callers triage mass evictions vs targeted preempts.
maria: Ops question: when we evict, do we flush KV/prefix caches or let them persist for fast reattach? Security-wise, caches should be tenant-isolated but still could leak if eviction reason is AUTHZ.
ken: Proposal: eviction has a boolean flag cache_invalidate: true/false. Default true for AUTHZ and CAPACITY_PREEMPT, false for graceful restart. Runtime must expose an idempotent invalidate API to cache subsystem: POST /internal/cache/invalidate {prefix:"/tenants/123/"}.
nash: Token scope note: claim token must encode resource pin (model_id + model_version) and allowed fallback variants. Do NOT let token allow arbitrary model substitution. Example claim token payload: 
```
{ "sub": "runtime-abcdef", "scope": ["model:rw:model-x:v3"], "mode": "dedicated", "claim_origin": "controlplane", "exp": 1825010599 }
```
ops-bot: deploybot: rolling out claim-renewal v2 to canary (arch-canary) at 2026-03-23T10:42Z :rocket:
ken: Eviction priority queue: when capacity is tight, evict by (SLA_rank, tenant_weight, connection_age). We should allow tenant-weight override via billing-tier tag.
tanvi: Note: KV cache flush on eviction can be expensive. Consider best-effort async invalidation plus a TTL on cached prefixes to avoid spikes.
maria: Decision (tentative): I'll write RFC with defaults: hosted TTL=90s, dedicated TTL=30s, private TTL=300s; renewal jitter; grace window=120s; structured headers + final stream event for hosted/dedicated; local journal + pull model for private; cache_invalidate flag and async invalidation recommended; token scope must include model pin. Reviewers: @ash @ken @tanvi.
nash: I can take a pass today. :thumbsup:
ken: Add me as reviewer too.
tanvi: I'll add notes about cache backpressure and async invalidation in the RFC.
maria: one more ops anchor: include a playbook entry for surge evictions (rate-limit claim renews on control plane side, exponential backoff on runtime).
ops-bot: incident-bot: FYI previous eviction surge traced to autoscaler bug on 2025-11-09 — see https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2025-11-09-eviction-surge for context.
ken: Acked. Also add a CLI check: `rwctl claim-status --runtime runtime-abcdef` that returns last renew, expiry, last_reason.
maria: Perfect. I'll open the RFC PR and tag reviewers. Thanks all.
